pairs.difference: Idli is white, made of rice and urad dal, and eaten with sambar; Dhokla is yellow, made of gram flour, and Gujarati.
Pav Bhaji comes with buttery mashed vegetables; Misal Pav comes with a fiery sprout curry topped with farsan.
Vada Pav has a fried potato fritter inside; Dabeli has a sweet-spicy potato mash with peanuts and pomegranate.
Pani Puri is filled with spiced water and eaten in one bite; Sev Puri is flat puris topped with sev and chutneys.
Dosa is thin and crispy; Uttapam is thick and soft with toppings cooked in.
Chole is made with chickpeas and usually eaten with bhature; Rajma is made with kidney beans and usually eaten with rice.
Biryani is layered, dum-cooked and spicier; Pulao is cooked in one pot and milder.
Naan is plain or buttered; Kulcha is softer, often stuffed, and Amritsari.
Poha is made of flattened rice and has peanuts; Upma is made of semolina.
A Cutlet is crumbed and eaten with ketchup; Aloo Tikki is a chaat, served with chole and chutneys.
Samosa is triangular with a potato filling; Kachori is round with a dal filling.
Butter Chicken comes in a creamy gravy; Tandoori Chicken is dry and charred from the tandoor.
Dal Makhani is creamy, black-lentil and North Indian; Sambar is tangy, has vegetables and is South Indian.
Noodles versus rice: you slurp one and spoon the other.
Roti is plain and everyday; Paratha is layered with ghee and often stuffed.
Khichdi is hot rice mashed with lentils; Curd Rice is cool rice mixed with yogurt.
Paneer Tikka is vegetarian cubes; Seekh Kebab is minced meat shaped around a skewer.
Rasam is a thin, peppery tamarind soup; Kadhi is thick, yellow and made from yogurt and gram flour.
Cauliflower balls versus paneer cubes, both Indo-Chinese.
Lemon Rice is yellow and tangy with peanuts; Jeera Rice is white and tastes of cumin.
Malai Kofta has fried paneer-potato balls in a creamy gravy; Dum Aloo is whole baby potatoes in a spicy gravy.
Pickle is sour, oily and kept in a jar; Papad is a thin crispy disc.
Eggs in gravy versus dry, crisp fried fish.
Bhature is puffed and deep-fried, from Punjab; Appam is a lacy rice pancake from Kerala.
Medu Vada is crisp, hot and eaten with sambar; Dahi Vada is soft, cold and soaked in yogurt.
Keema is minced meat; Palak Paneer is green spinach with paneer.
Momos are steamed dumplings; a Kathi Roll is a filling wrapped in a paratha.
Raita is cooling and made with yogurt; Chutney is a ground, often spicy paste.
One has egg; the other has vegetables, chutney and no egg.
Bhutta is roasted corn on the cob; Pakora is vegetables fried in batter. Both are monsoon snacks.
